industry.global: Global branded generics: ~US$394 bn in 2025, US$435 bn in 2026, ~10.7% CAGR to 2030 (Research and Markets via AR FY26). moatVerdict: Narrow moat: real but local. Ajanta's edge is speed to market with differentiated branded generics in small Indian therapy niches and in African/Asian markets where few Indian peers have field forces. It does not protect the US business (28% of sales), and the Indian niches are not deep: cardiology growth lagged the market in FY26 (7% vs 14%).

conflicts: Q1FY27 Asia sales: ₹255 cr in the press release and deck vs ₹225 cr in a transcript summary; Africa institutional ₹70 cr (deck) vs ₹49 cr (summary). We use the company's press release.
FY26 capex: ₹330 cr (company, MD&A and call) vs ₹365 cr (Screener cash flow, fixed assets purchased) vs ₹360 cr (ICICI Direct). We use the company figure in the text.
FY27 capex split: ₹250 cr expansion + ₹150 cr maintenance (5-May-2026 call) vs ₹300 cr + ₹100 cr (30-Jul-2026 call). We use the latest.
FY27 US filing target: 8-12 ANDAs (AR FY26, MOSL) vs 5-7 (Q1FY27 call per PL, BOBCAPS, ICICI Direct). We use 5-7 (latest).
PL's target: ₹3,730 on the cover, ₹3,725 in the text (32x FY28E). We use ₹3,730.
CARE puts FY26 revenue at ₹5,550 cr (total operating income on its own definition) vs ₹5,453 cr reported. We use the reported figure.
Screener classifies the FY26 mark-to-market hedge loss as an exceptional item (−₹73 cr after tax); the company reports no exceptional items. See the valuation chapter for how we treat it.
